name: BIO_do_connect_retry
prose: Retries BIO_do_connect on the given BIO until it succeeds, a timeout expires or a non-retryable error occurs. Precondition: bio may be NULL (checked); timeout is in seconds (timeout <= 0 selects blocking mode, timeout > 0 sets a deadline of now+timeout, max_time 0 means no deadline); a negative nap_milliseconds is replaced by 100. Postcondition: returns -1 after raising ERR_R_PASSED_NULL_PARAMETER if bio is NULL. Otherwise it sets the BIO non-blocking flag to (timeout > 0), sets an error-queue mark and calls BIO_do_connect. If that returns > 0 it clears the mark and returns that value. If it returns <= 0 and the last error is an ERR_LIB_BIO error with reason ERR_R_SYS_LIB, BIO_R_CONNECT_ERROR or BIO_R_NBIO_CONNECT_ERROR, it calls BIO_reset and treats the failure as retryable; otherwise retryability is BIO_should_retry. If timeout >= 0 and the failure is retryable it pops the error mark and calls the static bio_wait; a positive result loops back to retry, otherwise it raises BIO_R_CONNECT_TIMEOUT (wait result 0) or BIO_R_CONNECT_ERROR and returns that wait result (0 or -1). If timeout < 0 or the failure is not retryable, it clears the mark, returns -1 and raises BIO_R_CONNECT_ERROR only when the error queue had no entry. Note that with timeout == 0 bio_wait returns 1 immediately, so a retryable failure loops without a deadline.
note: slice cut the head: real function is BIO_do_connect_retry (bio_lib.c:1015); body read lines 1015-1078 plus bio_wait 953-987; the packet name bio_connect does not exist anywhere in the tree. Reasons were only mechanical name-not-in-slice.

name: acpt_state
prose: Runs the accept-BIO state machine on c->state until it reaches a return point. Precondition: b and c are non-NULL and c is the BIO_ACCEPT of b. Postcondition by state: ACPT_S_BEFORE fails with BIO_R_NO_ACCEPT_ADDR_OR_SERVICE_SPECIFIED (return -1) if both param_addr and param_serv are NULL, otherwise frees and NULLs the four cached name/service strings and moves to ACPT_S_GET_ADDR. ACPT_S_GET_ADDR maps accept_family to AF_INET6/AF_INET/AF_UNSPEC (unavailable or unsupported family raises an error and returns -1), calls BIO_lookup (failure returns -1) and returns -1 if the result list is empty, else moves to ACPT_S_CREATE_SOCKET. ACPT_S_CREATE_SOCKET tries BIO_socket on the current address; on failure it advances to the next address and retries, and if none remain raises BIO_R_UNABLE_TO_CREATE_SOCKET and returns -1; on success it stores the socket in c->accept_sock and b->num and moves to ACPT_S_LISTEN. ACPT_S_LISTEN calls BIO_listen and then BIO_sock_info; if either fails it closes accept_sock, sets accept_sock and b->num to INVALID_SOCKET and returns -1; on success it refreshes the cached accepting name/service, sets state ACPT_S_ACCEPT and returns 1 without accepting a connection. ACPT_S_ACCEPT: if b already has a next_bio it moves to ACPT_S_OK; otherwise it clears retry flags and cached peer strings and calls BIO_accept_ex. A negative result that BIO_sock_should_retry accepts sets the retry-special flag with retry_reason BIO_RR_ACCEPT and returns -1; any other negative result is returned as is and the listening socket is left open. On success it wraps the socket in a BIO_new_socket (BIO_CLOSE), copies b callbacks, optionally duplicates c->bio_chain and appends the socket to it, pushes the result onto b, caches the peer name/service, sets ACPT_S_OK and returns 1. Failures of BIO_new_socket, BIO_dup_chain, either BIO_push return -1 after the exit_loop cleanup, which frees the pending bio if there is one, else closes the accepted socket; when BIO_push(dbio, bio) fails the duplicated chain head dbio is not freed. ACPT_S_OK returns 1 if next_bio is set, else goes back to ACPT_S_ACCEPT. Any other state value returns 0.
note: bss_acpt.c:148-363 read fully. Reviewers: round-15 reason (this record) wrong on 2 of 3: ACPT_S_LISTEN falls through (245-254 no break) to 274-277 state=ACPT_S_ACCEPT, ret=1; default case returns 0 (350-352); right that accept failure leaves accept_sock open (298-310, exit_loop 356-360). Original reviewer (returns 1 on success, 0 means retry) wrong: retry returns -1 (151,302).

name: conn_state
prose: Runs the connect-BIO state machine on c->state, with b the BIO and c its BIO_CONNECT, until a state returns. Precondition: b and c are non-NULL. If c->info_callback is set it is called as cb(b, c->state, ret) after each state step that ends in a plain break (a zero result from it makes the function return 0 immediately) and once more at exit_loop, whose result is returned. Initial ret is -1. BIO_CONN_S_BEFORE: both hostname and service NULL raises an error and exits with ret -1 (state unchanged), else state becomes GET_ADDR. GET_ADDR: maps connect_family to AF_INET6/AF_INET/AF_UNSPEC (unavailable or unsupported family exits), calls BIO_lookup with connect_sock_type, and exits on lookup failure or an empty result (ret -1, state unchanged); else addr_iter = addr_first and state CREATE_SOCKET. CREATE_SOCKET: BIO_socket failure raises BIO_R_UNABLE_TO_CREATE_SOCKET and exits with ret equal to the failed socket value, state unchanged; success stores the socket in b->num and moves to CONNECT. CONNECT: clears retry flags, calls BIO_connect (adding BIO_SOCK_KEEPALIVE for SOCK_STREAM). If it returns 0 and BIO_sock_should_retry, it sets the retry-special flag, state BLOCKED_CONNECT, retry_reason BIO_RR_CONNECT and exits with ret 0; if it returns 0 and another address exists it closes the socket and goes back to CREATE_SOCKET; if it returns 0 with no more addresses it raises a sys error and sets state CONNECT_ERROR. A nonzero result goes on to conn_create_dgram_bio (which, for SOCK_DGRAM only, creates c->dgram_bio from b->num and on failure sets state CONNECT_ERROR) and then state OK. BLOCKED_CONNECT: if BIO_socket_wait on b->num returns 0 it just loops; else BIO_sock_error: nonzero moves to the next address (close socket, CREATE_SOCKET) or, with none left, raises BIO_R_NBIO_CONNECT_ERROR and exits with ret 0; zero goes through dgram creation to state OK. CONNECT_ERROR raises BIO_R_CONNECT_ERROR and exits with ret 0. OK exits with ret 1. An unrecognised state exits with whatever ret holds (-1 on a fresh call).
note: bss_conn.c:93-109 (conn_create_dgram_bio) and 111-283 read fully. Reviewer right: the early failures at 122-128, 158-168 and 177-183 do not set c->state to an error state. Reviewer wrong that the callback runs only at exit_loop: it also runs after each plain break at 271-274. (Original reason that is not in the packet fields was not shown; checked the above two.)

name: file_ctrl
prose: Control dispatcher of the file BIO. Precondition: b is non-NULL; for the seek, tell, eof and flush commands b->ptr must be a valid FILE * (or an uplink handle when BIO_FLAGS_UPLINK_INTERNAL is set); for BIO_C_SET_FILENAME ptr must be a NUL-terminated file name. The return value is a long chosen by cmd, defaulting to 1: BIO_C_FILE_SEEK and BIO_CTRL_RESET return the result of fseek(fp, num, 0) (0 on success, nonzero on failure); BIO_CTRL_EOF returns feof(fp); BIO_C_FILE_TELL and BIO_CTRL_INFO return ftell(fp) (on Windows builds -1 for a non-disk handle); BIO_C_SET_FILE_PTR calls file_free(b), sets b->shutdown to (num & BIO_CLOSE), b->ptr to ptr and b->init to 1, adjusts text/binary mode on some platforms, and returns 1; BIO_C_SET_FILENAME calls file_free(b), sets b->shutdown, builds the fopen mode from num (BIO_FP_APPEND, BIO_FP_READ, BIO_FP_WRITE) and, if no valid combination is set, raises BIO_R_BAD_FOPEN_MODE and returns 0; otherwise it calls openssl_fopen, and on failure raises sys/BIO errors and returns 0 with b->ptr and b->init not set by this call, while on success it stores the FILE in b->ptr, sets b->init to 1, clears BIO_FLAGS_UPLINK_INTERNAL and returns 1; BIO_C_GET_FILE_PTR stores b->ptr into *ptr when ptr is non-NULL and returns 1; BIO_CTRL_GET_CLOSE returns b->shutdown; BIO_CTRL_SET_CLOSE sets b->shutdown = num and returns 1; BIO_CTRL_FLUSH returns 1 if fflush does not return EOF, otherwise raises errors and returns 0; BIO_CTRL_DUP returns 1; BIO_CTRL_WPENDING, BIO_CTRL_PENDING, BIO_CTRL_PUSH, BIO_CTRL_POP and any unrecognised cmd return 0.
note: bss_file.c:179-348 read fully (file_free not read, so the state of b->ptr/init after file_free in the failure paths is left unspecified). Reviewers: original reviewer right that GET_CLOSE/PENDING returns and fopen/fflush failures were missing; round-15 reviewer right that init=1 is set only after a successful fopen (306-307, failure returns at 298-305).

name: BN_BLINDING_update
prose: Advances a BN_BLINDING after one use. Precondition: b and ctx are non-NULL. If b->A or b->Ai is NULL it raises BN_R_NOT_INITIALIZED and returns 0 (via the err label). Otherwise it sets counter to 0 if it was -1, then increments it. If the incremented counter equals BN_BLINDING_COUNTER and b->e is non-NULL and BN_BLINDING_NO_RECREATE is not set, it calls BN_BLINDING_create_param to regenerate A and Ai (return 0 if that fails). Otherwise, unless BN_BLINDING_NO_UPDATE is set, it squares Ai and A modulo b->mod (using bn_mul_mont_fixed_top when b->m_ctx is set, else BN_mod_mul), returning 0 if a multiplication fails; with NO_UPDATE set it leaves A and Ai untouched. On success it returns 1. At the err label, which both the success and failure paths reach, a counter equal to BN_BLINDING_COUNTER is reset to 0, so b->counter can change even on the NULL-A/Ai error path when the counter was already at that value.
note: bn_blind.c:91-124 read fully. Reviewer round-15 right: err label (120-122) resets counter==BN_BLINDING_COUNTER to 0 even on the NULL A/Ai error path. Original reviewer right: NO_UPDATE skips squaring (107) and re-creation needs e!=NULL and !NO_RECREATE (103).

name: bn_div_fixed_top
prose: Schoolbook long division of num by divisor that leaves its results in fixed-top form (not normalised). Precondition: num, divisor and ctx are valid, divisor->top > 0 with a non-zero top limb (asserted only in debug builds), dv and rm each NULL or a BIGNUM. It starts a BN_CTX frame, uses dv (or a ctx temporary when dv is NULL) as quotient, copies divisor into a temporary, left-aligns it (norm_shift) and clears its sign, and left-shifts num by norm_shift into a second temporary snum; if snum is not longer than the divisor it is zero-padded to div_n+1 limbs. It then computes loop = num_n - div_n quotient limbs, each by estimating q from the top limbs of the window, multiplying and subtracting the divisor, and adding it back if the estimate was too large. The quotient gets sign (num->neg XOR divisor->neg), top = loop and BN_FLG_FIXED_TOP; the remainder (snum, sign of num, top = div_n, FIXED_TOP) is shifted back right by norm_shift into rm when rm is non-NULL. Returns 1 on success; returns 0 if any ctx allocation, BN_copy, shift, or bn_wexpand fails, or if the final right shift into rm fails, ending the ctx frame in both cases. Neither the quotient nor the remainder is stripped of leading zero limbs and divisor zero is not checked here.
note: bn_div.c:266-461 read fully (slice cut the head; real name bn_div_fixed_top). Unreviewed before. Remainder written to rm only when rm != NULL (452); quotient is dv or a ctx temp (283); on failure after quotient setup dv may already be partly modified (329-335) so no claim of unchanged outputs.

name: BN_mod_inverse
prose: Public wrapper that solves a*x == 1 (mod n) by delegating to int_bn_mod_inverse. Precondition: a and n are valid BIGNUMs, in is NULL or a caller-owned BIGNUM for the result, ctx is NULL or a valid BN_CTX. If ctx is NULL it allocates a temporary one with BN_CTX_new_ex and, if that fails, raises ERR_R_BN_LIB and returns NULL. It then calls int_bn_mod_inverse with a local flag noinv initialised to 0; if the callee leaves noinv non-zero (it sets it to 1 for n == 0 or |n| == 1, and when the gcd of a and n is not 1) the wrapper raises BN_R_NO_INVERSE. It frees the temporary ctx (if it created one) and returns the callee result unchanged: the inverse, stored in in when in is non-NULL and otherwise in a newly allocated BIGNUM, or NULL on failure. Failures other than no-inverse (allocation or arithmetic errors inside the callee) return NULL without BN_R_NO_INVERSE being raised here.
note: slice cut the head and actually covers int_bn_mod_inverse (bn_gcd.c:~198-512); real function BN_mod_inverse is the wrapper at bn_gcd.c:515-535. Callee return/goto list read (206-208 n==0/1 sets *pnoinv=1; 492-503 gcd != 1 sets *pnoinv=1; err at 506-511); bn_mod_inverse_no_branch (215) not read, so noinv behaviour there is assumed only as the callee contract. Reviewer right that int_bn_mod_inverse itself raises no BN_R_NO_INVERSE and sets *pnoinv, wrapper raises at 531-532 and frees temp ctx at 533.

name: bn_mul_fixed_top
prose: Multiplies a by b into r and leaves r in fixed-top form. Precondition: a, b and r are valid BIGNUMs (r may be the same object as a or b) and ctx is a valid BN_CTX. If a->top or b->top is 0 it calls BN_zero(r) and returns 1 at once, without touching ctx. Otherwise it starts a ctx frame and, when r aliases a or b, computes into a ctx temporary rr (return 0 if the temporary cannot be obtained). It picks the algorithm by size: a Comba 8x8 multiply when both have 8 limbs (BN_MUL_COMBA builds), recursive Karatsuba (bn_mul_recursive or bn_mul_part_recursive) when both are at least BN_MULL_SIZE_NORMAL limbs and differ by at most one limb (BN_RECURSION builds), else schoolbook bn_mul_normal; each path grows the result with bn_wexpand and returns 0 if that fails. The result has top = a->top + b->top (not stripped of leading zeros), sign a->neg XOR b->neg and BN_FLG_FIXED_TOP; if a temporary was used it is copied into r with BN_copy (return 0 on failure). Returns 1 on success and ends the ctx frame at the err label, which both its success and error exits reach.
note: Round-15 had dropped this as name bn_mul; no function named bn_mul exists anywhere in crypto/bn or include/crypto/bn.h (only the file name). The slice contains the real function bn_mul_fixed_top (bn_mul.c:507-620, read fully), so FIX under that name per rule 6. Algorithm selection read at 540-605; BN_mul (wrapper) is not described here. No reviewer claims on this entry (mechanical only).

name: BN_mod_sqrt
prose: Tries to compute r with r^2 == a (mod p) by the Tonelli/Shanks method; p is expected to be prime but this is not checked beyond a few detections. Precondition: a, p valid BIGNUMs, in NULL or a caller-owned BIGNUM for the result, ctx a valid BN_CTX (used only past the first two special cases). Return: the root in in (if non-NULL) or a newly allocated BIGNUM, or NULL on failure. Early cases that do not touch ctx: if p is even or |p| == 1, then |p| == 2 gives r = (a & 1) (a mod 2 is not computed beyond testing bit 0), and any other such p raises BN_R_P_IS_NOT_PRIME and returns NULL; if a is exactly 0 or 1 the result is 0 or 1 (returned without reducing mod p). Otherwise A = a mod p is computed; with e the number of trailing zero bits of |p|-1 after the lowest: e == 1 uses a single modular exponentiation to (|p|+1)/4; e == 2 uses the Atkin formula; e > 2 searches y = 2..81 for a quadratic non-residue with BN_kronecker (small integers below 22, then random values), raising BN_R_P_IS_NOT_PRIME if the Kronecker symbol is 0 or y^q == 1 and BN_R_TOO_MANY_ITERATIONS if none is found, then runs the Shanks loop, which returns 0 when A is 0 mod p and raises BN_R_NOT_A_SQUARE when no suitable power of two exponent is found. Except for the 0-mod-p shortcut and the |p| == 2 and a in {0,1} cases, the result of the e == 1, e == 2 and Shanks paths is verified by squaring it mod p and comparing with A; a mismatch raises BN_R_NOT_A_SQUARE and returns NULL. On any failure after allocation a BIGNUM created here is freed with BN_clear_free, a caller-supplied in is not freed (but may already have been overwritten), and the ctx frame is ended.
note: bn_sqrt.c:13-367 read fully. Reviewer right: precondition "p odd" is too narrow because the |p|==2 case is handled at 28-41 (and other even p raise BN_R_P_IS_NOT_PRIME at 43). Verification step vrfy at 341-355 applies only on paths with goto vrfy (104,166,303); the a==0 mod p path (260-264,270-274) skips it.

name: DEFINE_OSSL_CMP_CTX_get1_certs(newChain)
prose: Generated function OSSL_CMP_CTX_get1_newChain (expanded from DEFINE_OSSL_CMP_CTX_get1_certs(newChain)). Returns an owned copy of the certificate stack ctx->newChain. If ctx is NULL it raises CMP_R_NULL_ARGUMENT and returns NULL. Otherwise it returns X509_chain_up_ref(ctx->newChain): a duplicate of the stack in which every certificate has its reference count incremented, which the caller must release (for example with OSSL_STACK_OF_X509_free). If ctx->newChain is NULL the duplicate is a new empty stack, not NULL; NULL is returned only when the stack duplication or one of the reference increments fails (in which case the partial copy is released).
note: macro-generated at cmp_ctx.c:455-463, instantiated at 466 (newChain) and 487 (extraCertsIn); X509_chain_up_ref read at x509_cmp.c:574-594 and OPENSSL_sk_dup at stack.c:48-76 (sk==NULL gives an empty stack). Reviewer right: a NULL field yields an empty stack, not NULL.

name: get_genm_itav
prose: Sends a GENM request carrying the ITAV req and returns the first ITAV of the GENP response whose infoType NID equals expected (desc names the type in log and error text). Precondition: req is an ITAV whose ownership is passed to this function; ctx is expected non-NULL with status OSSL_CMP_PKISTATUS_unspecified. If ctx is NULL (CMP_R_NULL_ARGUMENT) or its status is anything else (CMP_R_UNCLEAN_CTX), or OSSL_CMP_CTX_push0_genm_ITAV fails, it frees req and returns NULL. Once push0 succeeds ownership of req belongs to ctx, and req is not freed here on any later path. It then runs OSSL_CMP_exec_GENM_ses; if that returns NULL it returns NULL, raising CMP_R_GETTING_GENP only when ctx status is not OSSL_CMP_PKISTATUS_request (so no error is raised in that status). An empty response raises CMP_R_INVALID_GENP and returns NULL. Otherwise it shifts ITAVs off the response list one by one (logging a warning when there is more than one ITAV, and a warning for each non-matching infoType, freeing the non-matching ones); on the first match it frees the remaining ITAVs and the list and returns the matching ITAV, which the caller owns. If none matches it raises CMP_R_INVALID_GENP and returns NULL (the list is freed at the err label).
note: cmp_genm.c:74-139 read fully. Both reviewers right: returns NULL without raising an error when status is request (96-99); req is not freed on success paths because push0 transfers it to ctx (91-93), only err paths free it (135-138).

name: check_msg_all_certs
prose: Tries to find a sender certificate that authenticates msg and passes path validation, searching three certificate sources in turn. Precondition: ctx and msg are non-NULL; mode_3gpp is 0 for normal mode or non-zero for the exceptional 3GPP mode. If ctx->permitTAInExtraCertsForIR is set and the message body type is OSSL_CMP_PKIBODY_IP it only logs which mode it is trying; otherwise, if mode_3gpp is non-zero, it returns 0 immediately. It then calls check_msg_with_certs on msg->extraCerts, then on ctx->untrusted (skipping certs already checked from extraCerts), and returns 1 as soon as one of these succeeds. A call succeeds when some acceptable cert (per cert_acceptable) has a validated path (check_cert_path against ctx->trusted in normal mode, check_cert_path_3gpp in 3GPP mode) and ossl_cmp_ctx_set1_validatedSrvCert stores it in ctx. In 3GPP mode, path validation uses a store built only from self-issued extraCerts and, for an IP message, additionally requires that the newly enrolled certificate in the response also validates against that store. If both fail and ctx->trusted is NULL it logs a warning and returns 0; otherwise it runs check_msg_with_certs over all certificates of ctx->trusted (self-issued extraCerts description in 3GPP mode), frees that temporary stack and returns the result (1 or 0).
note: cmp_vfy.c:419-450 read fully, plus check_msg_with_certs (379-412) and check_cert_path_3gpp (327-364). Reviewer 1 right: early return 0 at 427-428 for mode_3gpp unless permitTAInExtraCertsForIR and IP body. Reviewer round-15 right: 3GPP validation also requires the newly enrolled cert to validate for IP (346-358). check_cert_path (normal mode) and cert_acceptable not read.

name: ossl_cms_env_asn1_ctrl
prose: Dispatches a CMS envelope control command (cmd) to the key-type specific handler for the recipient key. Precondition: ri is non-NULL. It selects the key: for CMS_RECIPINFO_TRANS the key is ri->d.ktri->pkey (not NULL-checked here); for CMS_RECIPINFO_AGREE it is the key of ri->d.kari->pctx, returning 0 if that pctx or its key is NULL; any other recipient type returns 0. For a DH or DHX key it returns the result of ossl_cms_dh_envelope(ri, cmd); for EC, ossl_cms_ecdh_envelope; for RSA, ossl_cms_rsa_envelope. For any other key type, if the key has no ameth or no ameth->pkey_ctrl it returns 1 without doing anything; otherwise it calls pkey_ctrl(pkey, ASN1_PKEY_CTRL_CMS_ENVELOPE, cmd, ri) and returns 0 with CMS_R_NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_THIS_KEY_TYPE if that returns -2, 0 with CMS_R_CTRL_FAILURE if it returns <= 0 (other than -2), and 1 otherwise.
note: cms_env.c:108-145 read fully; the three *_envelope handlers not read. Both reviewers right: the NULL pctx/pkey returns 0 at 117-121 and the 1 for a key without ameth/pkey_ctrl at 133-134 were omitted/contradicted by the old prose.

name: module_init
prose: Initialises one configuration module instance for pmod with the given name and value, and records it in the global initialized-modules list. Precondition: pmod, name, value are non-NULL (cnf is passed through to the module init callback). It allocates a CONF_IMODULE and duplicates name and value. If pmod->init is non-NULL it is called with the new imod and cnf; a result <= 0 is treated as failure. It then runs the one-time init of the list lock (failure is a failure), takes the RCU write lock, copies the current initialized_modules stack (or creates a new one), pushes imod, increments pmod->links, publishes the new stack, and after RCU synchronisation frees the old stack copy. On success it returns pmod->init result (a value > 0) or 1 when pmod->init is NULL. Failures return -1: allocation of imod, name or value fails (no finish call, no error raised here); init returns <= 0, the lock initialisation fails, or the stack copy or push fails (the latter two raise ERR_R_CRYPTO_LIB only for the copy/push). In the failure paths after init was called it calls pmod->finish(imod) when that callback is non-NULL, then frees imod and its strings; pmod->links is not incremented on failure.
note: conf_mod.c:427-505 read fully (slice real definition after the prototype at 81). Both reviewers right: the no-init path returns 1 (430, 489) and the RUN_ONCE failure returns -1 (458-459, 504), finish only if pmod->finish and init_called (494-495).

name: ossl_method_construct_precondition
prose: Decides whether methods for an operation should be constructed. Precondition: result may be NULL (checked); cbdata points to a construct_data_st (only its force_store field is read, through is_temporary_method_store); provider must be valid whenever the store is not temporary. The store is temporary exactly when no_store is non-zero and cbdata->force_store is zero. If result is NULL it raises ERR_R_PASSED_NULL_PARAMETER and returns 0. name: ossl_ec_GF2m_simple_oct2point
prose: Decodes the X9.62 octet string buf of length len into a point on a binary-field (GF(2^m)) curve. Precondition: group, point and buf are non-NULL and buf holds len bytes; ctx may be NULL (a temporary BN_CTX is then created in non-FIPS builds). Returns 0 with an error raised (EC_R_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL for len == 0) before anything else is touched. The first byte gives the form (0x00 infinity, 0x02/0x03 compressed, 0x04 uncompressed, 0x06/0x07 hybrid) and the low bit y_bit; any other form, or y_bit set with form 0 or 0x04, returns 0 (EC_R_INVALID_ENCODING). For form 0 the length must be exactly 1 and the result is EC_POINT_set_to_infinity(group, point). Otherwise len must equal 1 + field_len (compressed) or 1 + 2*field_len, with field_len = (degree+7)/8, else returns 0. It then reads x (and y for non-compressed forms) with BN_bin2bn, rejecting any coordinate with more than m bits; for compressed form it calls EC_POINT_set_compressed_coordinates with y_bit; for hybrid form it checks y_bit against x==0 (y_bit must be 0) or against the parity of y/x, returning 0 on mismatch; for uncompressed and hybrid forms it finally calls EC_POINT_set_affine_coordinates, which is relied on to check that the point is on the curve. Returns 1 only when that last step succeeds (or the infinity case), and 0 on any failure; the ctx frame and any temporary ctx are released on the paths after they were created (the early returns happen before they exist).

name: ossl_ec_key_public_check
prose: Full public key validation of an EC_KEY (SP 800-56A 5.6.2.3.3). Precondition: eckey must be non-NULL (it is dereferenced for eckey->group on the first line, before any NULL test), and its group and pub_key should be set; ctx is passed to the arithmetic. It first calls ossl_ec_key_public_check_quick, which returns 0 (with errors raised) if eckey, its group or its pub_key is NULL, the public point is infinity, its coordinates are out of range or it is not on the curve. If the group cofactor is non-NULL and equals 1 it returns 1 at that point without the order check. Otherwise it allocates a temporary point (returning 0 without raising an error here if EC_POINT_new fails), returns 0 with EC_R_INVALID_GROUP_ORDER if the group order is zero, computes pub_key * order with EC_POINT_mul (0 with ERR_R_EC_LIB if that fails), and returns 0 with EC_R_WRONG_ORDER unless that product is the point at infinity; otherwise returns 1. The temporary point is freed at the err label, which the success and error exits after its creation reach; the key is not modified.

name: EC_KEY_set_group
prose: Replaces the group of key with a duplicate of group. Precondition: key and group are non-NULL and key->meth is set. If key->meth->set_group exists and returns 0 it returns 0 and key is unchanged. Otherwise it releases the key old group reference with EC_GROUP_free(key->group), stores EC_GROUP_dup(group) as the new group (the result is not checked before the following step), and if that group is non-NULL and its curve name is NID_sm2 sets EC_FLAG_SM2_RANGE on the key. It then increments key->dirty_cnt unconditionally (also when the dup failed) and returns 0 if the duplicate is NULL (key->group is then NULL), else 1. The caller reference to group is not consumed; if group is the same object as key->group and the key held its only reference, freeing it before the dup happens first (line 772 before 773).

name: pkey_ec_ctrl
prose: Control dispatcher for the legacy EC EVP_PKEY method; ctx->data is the EC_PKEY_CTX. Return value by type: PARAMGEN_CURVE_NID looks up the curve p1 (EC_R_INVALID_CURVE and 0 if unknown), frees the old gen_group, stores the new one and returns 1. PARAM_ENC returns 0 with EC_R_NO_PARAMETERS_SET if gen_group is NULL, else sets its ASN1 flag to p1 and returns 1. ECDH_COFACTOR with p1 == -2 queries: returns cofactor_mode if it is not -1, otherwise 1 or 0 according to EC_FLAG_COFACTOR_ECDH on the pkey EC key. For other p1: values outside -1..1 return -2; otherwise cofactor_mode is set to p1 first, and then for p1 != -1 it returns 0 (ERR_R_UNSUPPORTED) if the pkey is a provided key (cofactor_mode stays changed), -2 if the EC key has no group, 1 if the group cofactor is 1, 0 if duplicating the key fails, else it sets or clears EC_FLAG_COFACTOR_ECDH on the duplicate co_key and returns 1; for p1 == -1 it frees co_key and returns 1. KDF_TYPE with p1 == -2 returns the current kdf_type; values other than NONE and X9_63 return -2, else stored and 1. KDF_MD stores p2 and returns 1; GET_EC_KDF_MD writes the kdf_md pointer to *p2 and returns 1. KDF_OUTLEN returns -2 if p1 <= 0, else stores it and returns 1; GET_EC_KDF_OUTLEN writes the outlen as int to *p2 and returns 1. KDF_UKM frees the previous kdf_ukm, takes ownership of p2 (pointer stored, length p1, or 0 if p2 is NULL) and returns 1; GET_EC_KDF_UKM writes the pointer to *p2 and returns kdf_ukmlen. CTRL_MD accepts only SHA-1, ECDSA-with-SHA1, SHA-2 and SHA-3 digests and SM3 (else EC_R_INVALID_DIGEST_TYPE and 0) and stores it, returning 1; GET_MD writes md to *p2 and returns 1. PEER_KEY, DIGESTINIT, PKCS7_SIGN and CMS_SIGN return 1 and do nothing; any other type returns -2.

name: decoder_process
prose: Recursive worker of the OSSL_DECODER chain, used both for the first call (params == NULL) and as the data callback that each decoder implementation calls with the object it decoded. Precondition: arg points to a decoder_process_data_st with valid ctx and bio. At entry it sets data->flag_next_level_called = 1 and remembers ctx->start_input_type. If params == NULL (first level) it sets current_decoder_inst_index to the number of decoders and does not touch flag_construct_called. Otherwise it picks the decoder instance at current_decoder_inst_index, clears flag_construct_called, and if ctx->construct is set calls it; a result > 0 sets flag_construct_called = 1 and the function returns 1 (end). If construct is absent or does not succeed it requires an OSSL_OBJECT_PARAM_DATA octet string in params (otherwise returns 0), wraps it in a new memory BIO, reads optional data type, data structure and input type parameters (a failed read returns 0), may overwrite ctx->start_input_type and set flag_input_structure_checked, and drops a "type-specific" data structure when a data type exists. It then returns 0 if no decoder instances remain below the current index, or if BIO_tell on the input fails or the core BIO cannot be created. Otherwise it walks the instances below the current index downwards, skipping each whose input type, data type, input structure or user-requested structure does not match; for a candidate it BIO_seek()s back to the saved position (returning the current ok value, without trying more, if BIO_tell then differs), sets a new recursion level and calls that decoder decode with decoder_process as callback, setting data->flag_construct_called from the recursive state. The loop stops after a decode that returned 0 or after a construct was called (error mark cleared), and after a decode that recursed (flag_next_level_called). The return value is the ok of the last decode attempted (so 1 can be returned when a decoder reported success without an object being constructed, and 0 when no instance matched or the last attempt failed). At the end label (which all exits go through) it frees the core BIO and the in-memory BIO it created (not the caller bio) and restores ctx->start_input_type.

name: encoder_process
prose: Recursive worker that selects a chain of encoder instances and runs them to produce the output. Precondition: data points to a valid encoder_process_data_st; the call with data->next_encoder_inst == NULL is the top level, which sets count_output_structure to -1 (no output structure requested) or 0 and writes its output to data->bio. The return value is 1 when an encoder ran successfully, 0 when a chosen encoder or its setup failed, and -1 when the instance lookup found nothing usable at this level (the caller then treats its own encoder as the first in the chain). It scans instances from index current_encoder_inst_index-1 downward; at the top level it skips instances whose output type differs from ctx->output_type, deeper it skips instances whose output type is not the name of the next encoder; if both ctx->output_structure and the instance structure are set it skips mismatches and counts matches. For each candidate it recurses; a recursive result of 0 is skipped and the scan continues, any other result stops the scan. If the scan ends without a candidate (including when a recursive failure was the last one tried) the function returns -1. Otherwise: for a recursive result of -1 it returns 0 at once if a structure was requested but none matched (count_output_structure == 0), else calls ctx->construct to build the object (NULL gives 0) and records the encoder name as data_type; for a recursive result of 1 it builds an object abstraction from the previous output (running_output) or, if that is NULL, raises an internal error and gives 0. If ok is non-zero it then encodes: at the top level into data->bio, deeper into a new memory BIO (failure to create it or the core BIO gives 0), and calls the instance encode. Finally it frees the previous running_output, hands the memory BIO contents (when one was created) to data->running_output, frees the BIO, calls ctx->cleanup when an object was constructed, and returns ok. At the top level on success running_output is therefore NULL after return.

name: ENGINE_ctrl_cmd
prose: Runs the named control command of an ENGINE with a numeric argument i, pointer p and function pointer f. Precondition: e and cmd_name are non-NULL, otherwise it raises ERR_R_PASSED_NULL_PARAMETER and returns 0. It resolves the command number with ENGINE_ctrl(e, ENGINE_CTRL_GET_CMD_FROM_NAME, 0, cmd_name, NULL). If e->ctrl is NULL or the lookup returns <= 0 (command unknown), then when cmd_optional is non-zero it clears the error queue and returns 1 (pretending success), and otherwise raises ENGINE_R_INVALID_CMD_NAME and returns 0. If the command is found it calls ENGINE_ctrl(e, num, i, p, f) and returns 1 if that result is > 0 and 0 otherwise; the engine own return value is not passed back. It does not check whether the command is executable.

name: enc_ctrl
prose: Control dispatcher of the cipher filter BIO. Precondition: b is non-NULL; if its BIO_ENC_CTX data is NULL it returns 0 at once. Default return value is 1. BIO_CTRL_RESET sets ok = 1 and finished = 0, re-initialises the cipher keeping the current direction (returning 0 if EVP_CipherInit_ex fails) and otherwise returns the result of BIO_ctrl on the next BIO. BIO_CTRL_EOF returns 1 when ctx->cont <= 0, else the next BIO result. BIO_CTRL_WPENDING and BIO_CTRL_PENDING return buf_len - buf_off if that is positive, otherwise the next BIO result. BIO_CTRL_FLUSH first loops calling enc_write(b, NULL, 0) while buffered bytes remain, returning that call result i if it is negative or if no bytes were written in the call; then, if not yet finished, marks finished, calls EVP_CipherFinal_ex into the buffer and stores its result in ctx->ok (a result <= 0 is returned as the control result without flushing further), writes out the final bytes by repeating the loop, and finally flushes the next BIO, returning its result and copying its retry flags. BIO_C_GET_CIPHER_STATUS returns ctx->ok. BIO_C_DO_STATE_MACHINE clears retry flags, forwards to the next BIO, and copies its retry flags. BIO_C_GET_CIPHER_CTX stores ctx->cipher in *ptr, marks the BIO initialised and returns 1. BIO_CTRL_DUP allocates a cipher context in the duplicate BIO data (returning 0 if that fails), copies the cipher context into it and returns the copy result, marking the duplicate initialised if it succeeded. Any other command is forwarded to the next BIO.
